audit_findings.title: The cash and liability bridge predates the completed WTech acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $394 million cash paid at closing, equal to $0.87 per diluted share and 3.4% of the $11,448 million base equity value; other effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-closing bridge should reduce cash for consideration paid and include any acquired cash, new financing claims, transaction costs and incremental interest in owner earnings, while also recognizing WTech's operating contribution.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions and investments may involve significant cash expenditures, the incurrence of debt, expenses, and operating losses that could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The stale bridge is a demonstrated error: the valuation adds June 30 cash even though APG paid $394 million for WTech on July 1. The known cash adjustment alone would lower base value from $25.31 to approximately $24.44 per share and would not reverse the conclusion relative to the $40.04 market price. The net error remains uncertain because WTech earnings, acquired cash, fees and post-closing financing effects were not supplied and could offset or enlarge the reduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the WTech purchase-price allocation, acquired cash, transaction fees and financing records; construct a July 1 pro-forma bridge and rerun owner earnings with WTech earnings and incremental interest included consistently.

audit_findings.title: The Series A year-end dividend remains a variable claim not fixed by the supplied denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: 3.159305 million provisional dividend-equivalent shares; at the $40.04 valuation price the filed formula computes to approximately $52.1 million, or about 1.30 million shares if issued at that price; final variance unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The final Series A dividend changes the fully diluted share denominator if paid in shares or creates a cash claim on equity if paid in cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Annual Dividend Amount is equal to 20 % of the increase in the volume-weighted average market price per share of the Company’s common shares for the last ten trading days of the calendar year, multiplied by 211,791,957 shares.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved measurement issue, not a demonstrated final dilution error. The obligation depends on the last-ten-trading-day 2026 VWAP and the settlement election, neither of which was known on September 5. Actual dilution could be above or below the 3.159305 million provisional shares, so the direction and materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: After year-end, calculate the dividend using the actual ten-day VWAP, confirm entitlement through the December 31 conversion and the cash-versus-share election, then replace the provisional equivalent with the actual obligation and rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $186 million of acquisition cash in 2025 and $778 million in 2024, totaling $964 million; the modeled growth premium over the bear case is $3,398 million in the base case and $4,622 million in the bull case
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings can raise the historical owner-earnings trend and modeled growth even though the acquisition cash required to obtain those earnings is outside operating cash flow and maintenance capital expenditure.
audit_findings.evidence: We had cash used in acquisitions, net of cash acquired of $186 million and $778 million in the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate substantial acquisition spending, while the record does not separate acquired from organic growth. Because the 7%-9% assumptions create $3.4-$4.6 billion of value above the zero-growth case, dependence on undeducted acquisition investment is reasonably capable of materially overstating the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual organic-versus-acquired revenue and owner-earnings bridge for every trend year; rerun growth using supported organic growth or deduct the normalized acquisition investment required to deliver the modeled growth.

audit_findings.title: Potential multiemployer-pension withdrawal claims are unrecorded
audit_findings.mechanism: A withdrawal or mass-withdrawal liability would be a claim ahead of common equity and could also reduce future owner earnings through payments or higher contributions.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to uncertainty regarding future factors that could trigger withdrawal liability, as well as the absence of specific information regarding the MEPPs current financial situation, the Company is unable to determine (a) the amount and timing of any future withdrawal liability, if any, and (b) whether the Company’s participation in these MEPPs could have a material adverse impact on the Company’s consolidated financial position, results of operations, or liquidity.
audit_findings.explanation: No withdrawal liability was recorded, and the company states that neither its amount nor timing can be determined. Filed contributions of $99 million in 2025 and $54 million in the first half of 2026 demonstrate meaningful participation but do not measure withdrawal exposure. The red-zone plan and significant-contributor disclosures make the possibility relevant, while the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current funding notices, Forms 5500, employer withdrawal estimates and contemplated restructuring or acquisition actions; add a bridge claim or probability-weighted scenario only when a supportable exposure is available.

audit_findings.title: Deferred acquisition consideration is omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $45 million deferred-payment liability at June 30, 2026, equal to approximately $0.10 per diluted share and 0.4% of the $11,448 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid purchase consideration is an equity claim when its eventual payment is outside owner earnings; employment-linked compensation already expensed should not be deducted again.
audit_findings.evidence: The total liability for deferred payments was $ 39 and $ 28 at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and is included in contingent consideration and compensation liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets for all periods presented.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $45 million deferred-payment liability absent from the stated bridge. Its full deduction would reduce base value only from $25.31 to approximately $25.21 per share and cannot change the conclusion relative to the $40.04 market price. The separate $17 million contingent-consideration balance should still be classified consistently but is also small at this valuation scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $45 million deferred payments and $17 million contingent consideration to the June 30 liability accounts; deduct only unpaid purchase-price claims not captured in owner earnings and exclude compensation already expensed.

audit_findings.title: Not all reported cash may be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $851 million cash addition, equal to $1.88 per diluted share and 7.4% of the $11,448 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Only cash transferable to common shareholders after operating, legal, tax, collateral and transaction requirements belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, there were accumulated undistributed earnings of subsidiaries outside of the United States, all of which are considered to be indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not identify the restricted or operational portion of cash, so the precise overstatement is unresolved. Nevertheless, even removing the entire $851 million cash balance would reduce base value only to approximately $23.43 per share, still well below the $40.04 market price; therefore this issue alone cannot change the valuation conclusion. WTech's specifically identified closing use is assessed separately in finding 1.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 30 and post-WTech cash schedule by jurisdiction and legal entity, identifying restricted, collateral, operating and transaction-committed balances; retain only demonstrably excess distributable cash in the next rerun.
